title: Temperance: Adjusting the Mix So Different Needs Can Work Together

quickTake.upright: Don't use all your energy in one burst. Adjust proportions and pace to help things run more smoothly.
quickTake.reversed: The mix or rhythm is off. First find what there is too much of, and what is missing.

introMarkdown:
Upright in a sentence: Don't use all your energy in one burst. Adjust proportions and pace to help things run more smoothly.

Reversed in a sentence: The mix or rhythm is off. First find what there is too much of, and what is missing.

Water is still flowing between the two cups. Temperance concerns ongoing adjustment: how to combine time, energy, and needs so something can last.

sections.title: Adjusting Water by Hand, Standing in Two Places
sections.bodyMarkdown:
A white-robed angel spreads red wings, eyes lowered toward two gold cups held at different heights. A diagonal blue stream connects them. A dot-in-circle symbol appears on the forehead with rays around it. On the chest, an upward triangle sits inside a square, with lettering visible above.

One foot stands in water, the other on the bank, rather than the feet being together. Yellow flowers and long green leaves grow on the right. On the left, a path winds through green rises toward blue mountains, with yellow radiance beyond. The figure is steady, yet neither cups nor feet are arranged in perfect symmetry. Maintaining this posture needs continuing coordination. [View the card image used in this article](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:RWS_Tarot_14_Temperance.jpg)

The cups do not simply each hold half the water, nor are water and land mixed into one beneath the feet. The picture can remind us that cooperation may preserve difference, and harmonizing remains a process. Following the narrow stream to the distant path shows that small present adjustments and a longer direction can coexist. A modern application might change one proportion and observe the result rather than reorganizing an entire life at once. The stream's direction belongs to a symbolic image; it requires no invented physical mechanism. Symbols on forehead and chest also cannot reveal a personal medication dose or bodily measurement.

sections.title: Harmonizing Is an Active Process
sections.bodyMarkdown: Waite calls the flow between the cups a pouring of the essences of life, and explains that although he uses a masculine pronoun, the angel is neither male nor female. He places the feet on land and water, distant light, and crown within religious symbolism of life, ending with the harmonizing of spiritual and material natures. The distant crown is unclear in the scan, so it is presented here as Waite's interpretation rather than something everyone can immediately see. [Waite, Part II, XIV](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pktar14.htm)

sections.title: Upright: Adjust Gradually Toward Something Sustainable
sections.bodyMarkdown:
This site uses Temperance to discuss proportion and coordination. You do not need to do the maximum every time. Observe what a little more or less changes, then find a mix suited to current conditions. Study and rest, speaking and listening, planning and flexibility may all need this back-and-forth adjustment.

Two coexisting needs do not mean an equal half is automatically fair. Sometimes the more urgent side must be handled first, then recovery arranged for the other. What matters is continuing to see the whole, rather than treating one number as a permanently correct standard.

sections.title: Reversed: Locate the Actual Mismatch
sections.bodyMarkdown:
Reversal can suggest unbalanced investment, incompatible ways of collaborating, or too many changes scattering the rhythm. Ask which two parts fail to connect: conflicting schedules, missing handover information, or constant swings between rushing and complete stoppage?

Waite's upright list includes moderation and management; reversal includes disunion and competing interests, alongside older associations such as religious institutions. This article uses the former as reading cues without reducing the whole card to a health diagnosis. Temperance cannot decide medication doses, dietary restrictions, or treatment plans for you. [Waite, Part III, §3, entry 14](https://original.sacred-texts.com/tarot/pkt/pkt0303.htm)

sections.title: Distinguishing Related Meanings
sections.bodyMarkdown: Temperance and Justice are both easily summarized as balance. Justice looks more at whether standards and responsibilities are reasonable; Temperance asks how different parts connect in operation. Compared with Strength, Temperance need not involve steadying a reaction in an intense moment. It may be the repeated adjustment of time across an ordinary week. In reversal, break “everything has been chaotic” into specific conflicts: starting too late, too little handover information, or changing too much at once? Alter only one observable condition at a time to identify what genuinely helps. When a request crosses a threshold of safety or respect, refusal is more appropriate than compromise.

sections.title: Learning a Language Together Without Sharing One Speed
sections.bodyMarkdown:
**Original fictional case.** Qingqing asks, “My friend and I meet to practice conversation. How can we keep it up?”

Known facts: She wants to correct pronunciation slowly, while her friend wants more discussion of content. Every session becomes an argument between correction and free conversation. Both still want to continue and have a regular half hour each week. She draws upright Temperance in the collaboration-advice position.

The movement between two cups can inspire a process linking different goals, while feet on land and water acknowledge both needs. The problem has a clear scope: not whose learning style is more correct, but how thirty minutes can accommodate accuracy and fluency. Upright Temperance suits designing an adjustable proportion without requiring both interests to become the same goal.

Another possibility: If her friend does not actually want to continue and is simply embarrassed to refuse, dividing time will not solve willingness. If their levels differ too greatly, they may need more suitable practice partners; “accommodate each other” cannot bear every difference.

A practical next step: Try twenty minutes of free conversation followed by ten minutes of feedback on only two pronunciation points. After two weeks, each names one helpful and one uncomfortable aspect. Then decide whether to alter the proportion, change content, or practice separately, making sustained participation an observable result.

sections.title: Swinging Between Constant Replies and Total Disconnection
sections.bodyMarkdown:
**Original fictional case.** Jiamu asks, “I'm either answering messages nonstop or turning them off and forgetting to check all day. How can I adjust?”

Known facts: He works on an amateur theater production, needing both to respond to rehearsal changes and to reserve uninterrupted time for scenery drawings. All messages currently use the same alert, mixing ordinary chat with same-day changes. He draws reversed Temperance in the source-of-imbalance position.

Reversal fits two needs without an appropriate connection. The narrow stream between higher and lower cups suggests rhythmic information exchange, rather than simply “look at your phone less.” Messages he must answer genuinely affect others, and focus time genuinely matters. Treating everything as equally urgent causes the alternation between all-on and all-off.

Another possibility: If the theater group demands constant availability without a reasonable response window, renegotiation is needed rather than further personal optimization to accommodate unlimited demands. If message volume is actually low, he may simply have failed to set clear checking times.

A practical next step: Distinguish same-day changes from ordinary discussion with the team and agree on a contact method for urgent matters. Schedule several regular checking windows each day, concentrating on drawings in between. After a week, check whether important information was missed and adjust frequency, rather than aiming never to be interrupted.

sections.title: Practice: Make One Small Adjustment
sections.bodyMarkdown: Choose two needs that repeatedly conflict, such as quiet work and prompt replies. Describe the present situation, then try one small change: several fixed reply windows daily, with notifications off at other times. After a week, see whether both work and communication improved before deciding to keep or revise it.

sections.bodyMarkdown: Temperance does not mean always doing less, suppressing desire, or compromising in every conflict. It concerns a suitable combination. When a request crosses a limit of safety or respect, a clear refusal can also help restore a sustainable life.
